cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived in the geological past

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: Modes of preservation: original material (amber, freezing), replacement (petrification), permineralisation (mineral-filled pores), mould and cast, compression (carbon film)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: Trace fossils preserve evidence of activity: footprints, burrows, coprolites, rather than the organism itself

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: Body fossils preserve part of the organism: shells, bones, teeth, soft tissues (rare)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: Fossils indicate palaeoenvironments: coral = warm shallow sea; ferns = humid land; glacial deposits = cold climate

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fossils & Palaeontology
cards.back: The fossil record is incomplete because most organisms decompose before fossilisation can occur

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — fossils & palaeontology?
cards.back: 1. For Fossils & Palaeontology questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Fossils & Palaeontology to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
Describe the different modes of fossil preservation and explain how fossils are used to reconstruct past environments. [6 marks]
